name: clipzyme_reactzyme_reaction_similarity_baseline_contract_v1

authoritative_external_baseline.name: CLIPZyme
authoritative_external_baseline.paper: CLIPZyme: Reaction-Conditioned Virtual Screening of Enzymes
authoritative_external_baseline.execution_boundary: The released CLIPZyme pseudo-transition/difference-graph reaction encoder requires directed substrate>>product atom-mapped reactions. ReactZyme reaction_smi_split supplies unordered dot-separated molecule bags, so direct use would invent unavailable directionality. For this contract only, freeze the literature-defined ReactZyme-protocol CLIPZyme variant: MAT-2D reaction encoder + ESM enzyme encoder, lightweight MLP projections, temperature-scaled cosine similarity, symmetric bidirectional InfoNCE with in-batch negatives.
authoritative_external_baseline.official_checkpoint_role: The released CLIPZyme checkpoint remains the authoritative native CLIPZyme asset for directed reaction inputs, but is not applied to unordered ReactZyme molecule bags.

tiger_reference.name: TIGER
tiger_reference.reason_not_selected: No official executable implementation or clean independent reproduction is available as of 2026-09-01.

baseline_native_inputs.reaction_encoder: ReactZyme-author MAT-2D scope adaptation for unordered molecule bags
baseline_native_inputs.directed_clipzyme_checkpoint_native_inpu: directed atom-mapped reactants>>products; incompatible with reaction_smi molecule-bag identity without invented directionality

support_freeze_rule.reaction_requirement: every molecule token must be parseable by the ReactZyme-author MAT-2D preprocessing; no substrate/product direction is invented
support_freeze_rule.protein_requirement: sequence accepted by the ReactZyme-author ESM preprocessing; author truncation policy retained
support_freeze_rule.pair_support: native ReactZyme positive/support identity intersected only with author encoder input support

metrics.query_semantics: R2E and E2R are reported separately on the same native score matrix. Hit@K is any-positive-in-top-K. Local MRR is standard best-positive reciprocal rank. If reproducing a paper implementation with a different positive-averaged reciprocal-rank convention, it must be reported as a separately named metric and never aliased to standard MRR.

benchmark_reveal_state.role: descriptive authoritative-baseline alignment plus coverage/capability evidence

allowed_adaptation: ReactZyme-protocol MAT-2D reaction encoder substituted solely because native reaction_smi inputs have no substrate/product direction
lightweight MLP projection heads and symmetric InfoNCE-style training defined before performance
metric wrapper on the unchanged native score matrix
forbidden_adaptation: inventing substrate/product direction or atom mapping for unordered ReactZyme molecule bags
Catalyst RDKit+, reaction-center, EnzGFM or ESM-C features inside the baseline
hand-designed target-specific negative mining beyond in-batch negatives
sweeping UniMol versus MAT or projection architectures on revealed test metrics
TIGER paper result substitution as the baseline

asset_acquisition.mat_checkpoint: ReactZyme points to the official MAT pretrained weights; acquire checksum-preserving copy before feature generation.
asset_acquisition.esm_checkpoint: ReactZyme process_esm.py specifies esm2_t33_650M_UR50D.pt; acquire official ESM asset if not already cached.
asset_acquisition.reason: scope-adapted baseline encodes the native ReactZyme test sequences directly with the author ESM pipeline; CLIPZyme screening_set is not needed.

scope_adaptation.reason: input-domain compatibility only, fixed before any new baseline performance
scope_adaptation.source_evidence: TIGER Appendix E describes CLIPZyme ii under ReactZyme protocol as MAT-2D (reaction) + ESM (enzyme), with lightweight MLP heads, temperature-scaled cosine similarity and symmetric InfoNCE-style bidirectional contrastive training. TIGER is methodology context only, not the baseline.
scope_adaptation.reaction_input_semantics: ReactZyme reaction_smi_split is an unordered dot-separated molecule bag. Wildcard * is normalized to carbon following ReactZyme author preprocessing; molecule order is not interpreted as substrate/product direction.
scope_adaptation.reaction_encoder: ReactZyme author MAT-2D preprocessing/model; per-molecule MAT representations pooled to a reaction-bag vector exactly as author process_mat.py does.
scope_adaptation.enzyme_encoder: ESM-2 t33 650M mean representation following ReactZyme author process_esm.py; sequence truncation <=5000 as author code.
scope_adaptation.projection_and_objective: one fixed lightweight MLP projection per modality into a shared normalized latent space; symmetric multi-positive InfoNCE with in-batch negatives; no hand-generated negative-pair dataset
scope_adaptation.selection: single preregistered MAT-2D+ESM variant selected for native input compatibility and locally auditable author code, not for target performance; no UniMol/MAT sweep
scope_adaptation.test_support: full native 14,688 unique protein x 386 unseen reaction matrix unless author encoder parsing itself fails; any failures are reported, not repaired with Catalyst features
